item.title: US Education Dept panel on law school accreditation hits impasse on ABA role
item.description: An appointee of President Donald Trump will determine whether to end the American Bar Association's status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools after a US Education Department panel failed to deliver a recommendation on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: An appointee of President Donald Trump will determine whether to end the American Bar Association's status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools after a US Education Department panel failed to deliver a recommendation on Thursday. An 18-member agency advisory committee deadlocked on the question after a full day of debate on Wednesday that was marked by complaints of political interference and uneven rule enforcement. Education Department Under Secretary Nicholas Kent is expected to make the final call on the ABA legal education council’s accreditor recognition in the coming months. “We take accreditation and our recognition as an accreditor very seriously,” Melissa Hart, chair of the ABA’s legal education council, said in a statement on Thursday. "We will continue to work cooperatively with the Department as the recognition process continues.” The Education Department said it would not comment while a decision is pending. The standoff over accreditation comes amid a wider political conflict surrounding both the ABA — the country's most-recognized attorney organization with about 150,000 dues-paying members — and its legal education council, which largely operates separately. The Education Department in August [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"recommended against"] renewing the ABA’s accreditor status, concluding that the legal education council is not "separate and independent" from the larger ABA as required. The staff report also faulted the ABA for being too slow to revise requirements related to law schools' diversity policies. Trump signed an executive order in April 2025 directing Education Secretary Linda McMahon to assess whether to [USN:L1N3R2130 TEXT:"suspend or terminate"] the ABA as the government’s official law school accreditor, citing its “unlawful" DEI requirements. Under rules the ABA repealed earlier this month, its accredited schools were required to demonstrate their commitment to diversity in recruitment, admissions and student programming. During debates on Wednesday before the Education Department's National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity, ABA critics on the committee argued that the real-world impact of ending its accreditor status would be modest because only five law schools rely on the ABA for access to federal student loans. ABA supporters countered that it would upend US legal education by creating a patchwork of state lawyer licensing rules and argued that the government's accreditation standards were being unevenly applied to single out the ABA. Read more: [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"Trump administration moves to end attorney group's law school oversight"] [USN:L1N3R2130 TEXT:"Trump executive order says ABA's role as law school accreditor may be revoked"]

item.title: Vídeo não mostra presidente do Paraguai agradecendo a Lula por empresas deixarem o Brasil
item.description: Um vídeo no qual o senador paraguaio Beto Ovelar conversa com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sobre um programa de transferência de renda circula nas redes sociais como se mostrasse o presidente do Paraguai, Santiago Peña, agradecendo a Lula por empresas terem migrado do Brasil para o país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo no qual o senador paraguaio Beto Ovelar conversa com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sobre um programa de transferência de renda circula nas redes sociais como se mostrasse o presidente do Paraguai, Santiago Peña, agradecendo a Lula por empresas terem migrado do Brasil para o país. Estes são os principais detalhes: “Lula foge de Rubio na ONU, mas é barrado pelo presidente do Paraguai, que agradece a política que faz empresas brasileiras atravessarem a fronteira”, dizem publicações no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads com a filmagem. Nesta semana, Lula participou da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, onde não se reuniu com o secretário de Estado norte-americano, Marco Rubio. Já o conteúdo checado foi postado por Ovelar em suas redes sociais em 30 de junho, quando o Paraguai sediou a cúpula do Mercosul , evento que teve a presença de Lula. É possível ouvir no vídeo que Ovelar falava, em espanhol, sobre o auxílio de Lula na criação do Tekoporã , um programa social no Paraguai semelhante ao Bolsa Família . "Quando o senhor foi presidente da República, eu era ministro , e o senhor abriu as portas do Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social. Hoje, nós temos um programa que se chama Tekoporã, e, graças à abertura do senhor, isso foi possível", disse. Veredicto: Legenda errada. O vídeo mostra um senador do Paraguai agradecendo a Lula pela ajuda na criação de um programa social, e não pela migração de empresas brasileiras para o país. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Zidane relata "emoção imensa" antes de primeira partida no comando da França
item.description: Zinedine Zidane falou sobre sua “emoção imensa” ao se preparar para assumir o comando da França pela primeira vez na estreia da Liga das Nações, fora de casa, contra a Turquia, na sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zinedine Zidane falou sobre sua “emoção imensa” ao se preparar para assumir o comando da França pela primeira vez na estreia da Liga das Nações, fora de casa, contra a Turquia, na sexta-feira. O técnico de 54 anos, que sucedeu Didier Deschamps após o reinado de 14 anos de seu antecessor, inicia sua passagem com uma partida fora de casa em Kocaeli, menos de dois meses após sua nomeação. “Talvez até mais, na verdade”, disse Zidane quando questionado se suas emoções se comparavam às que sentiu ao estrear pela seleção francesa, há 32 anos. “Foi há muito tempo, e hoje sinto uma emoção imensa por estar aqui no comando desta seleção francesa”, declarou ele em uma coletiva de imprensa. A nomeação de Zidane gerou grande entusiasmo na França, onde sua primeira semana no comando dominou a cobertura da mídia, e na Turquia, onde um jornalista chegou a pedir um autógrafo a ele durante a coletiva de imprensa. O ex-técnico do Real Madrid, no entanto, procurou manter o foco em seu elenco. “É o próximo passo após os 14 anos de Didier; é algo novo, então é completamente normal. Mas os principais protagonistas são os jogadores”, disse ele. “Acho que a gente só precisa aceitar como as coisas são feitas; não estou atrás disso e não estou aqui por isso. Vou tentar fazer meu trabalho com meus jogadores, para garantir que possamos vencer as partidas – é isso que me interessa.” O meio-campista Adrien Rabiot disse que Zidane tentou “se afastar o máximo possível para deixar os jogadores se expressarem”. “Ele é conosco do mesmo jeito que é fora do time”, acrescentou Rabiot. “Estamos plenamente cientes da importância que ele tem para o futebol francês. Sua aura faz com que ele ocupe muito espaço e as pessoas esperem muito dele.” Rabiot, nomeado um dos capitães da equipe ao lado de Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé e Jules Koundé, observou que “muitas coisas mudaram” desde que Zidane substituiu Deschamps. “Já há alguns jogadores novos, maneiras diferentes de fazer as coisas e também treinos diferentes”, disse o vice-campeão da Copa do Mundo de 2022. “O que o técnico quer é, obviamente, um estilo de jogo bastante ofensivo." A França enfrenta mais uma partida fora de casa contra a Bélgica na segunda-feira, antes do primeiro jogo em casa de Zidane, contra a Itália, na próxima sexta-feira.

item.title: Infantino looks set to stay, but FIFA faces a new war over power
item.description: The battle to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA may be nearly all over just a few weeks after his opponents thought they would dethrone the president of world soccer's governing body, but the war over how much power he can exercise may only be beginning.
item.dc:creator: Julien Pretot
item.content:encoded: The battle to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA may be nearly all over just a few weeks after his opponents thought they would [USN:L6N44H116 TEXT:"dethrone"] the president of world soccer's governing body, but the war over how much power he can exercise may only be beginning. Senior figures in world football increasingly see the crisis triggered by Infantino's abandoned private-investment plan shifting away from the question of succession and towards a struggle over the terms of his continued presidency. One outcome could be a governance compromise under which Infantino remains in office but gives up some power. The other possibility is a prolonged “hot-cold war” in which clubs, confederations, player representatives and national associations challenge FIFA repeatedly over competitions, money and control of the international calendar. “What is clear now ... is that he’s going nowhere,” a senior world football executive told Reuters. “A hot-cold war is a very real problem for FIFA and for world football.” A veteran international sports executive, who has spent decades working with governing bodies, offered a similar assessment, saying Infantino was “hanging on” but questioning how FIFA could operate if many of the game’s most powerful countries and institutions remained opposed to him. “You would have effectively a civil war within the governance which I cannot recall in a sports body before,” the executive said. “Unprecedented.” That possible scenario of a prolonged and potentially damaging cold war within world football was independently corroborated to Reuters by two other senior football officials. The prospect points to a potentially paradoxical outcome to a crisis that at its height threatened Infantino’s position: he could survive politically while presiding over a governing body in which some of football’s biggest stakeholders seek to constrain what he can actually do. “Does he become a lame duck?” the veteran executive asked. TRUST STILL BROKEN There is little indication that Infantino’s attempt this week to draw a line under the crisis has repaired the rupture. In a letter to the FIFA Council and the presidents of all 211 member associations, Infantino proposed that the Council consider commissioning an [USN:L1N45D0SB TEXT:"independent external review"] of FIFA’s governance framework for major strategic initiatives. He also proposed consultations with confederations, associations and other stakeholders over strengthening decision-making and said he remained fully committed to leading FIFA. Several European federations quickly [USN:L6N45E0RY TEXT:"dismissed"] the move, and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin issued a [USN:L6N45F0FH TEXT:"stern assessment"] on Wednesday. “The project that shattered the unity of world football may be abolished, but the trust it broke has not returned,” Ceferin said in a video address to the Portugal Football Summit. “Trust in our sport rests on three pillars: unity, transparency, and governance that serves the many, not the few.” “Football is not for sale,” he added. Ceferin did not name Infantino but his remarks were a clear reference to the proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA’s commercial rights, including rights linked to the World Cup, to private investors. The project was dropped in July after opposition from European soccer's governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North American confederation CONCACAF. ATTRITION For 56-year-old Swiss-Italian Infantino, that leaves one route to a less confrontational settlement, which is a reform substantial enough to persuade his opponents that power inside FIFA has genuinely shifted. The senior world football executive said one possible outcome could be the creation of a new body or structure that diluted the authority of the president. Infantino’s governance proposals were the “bare minimum” needed to give him room to remain in office, the executive said, adding that the question was whether he would accept meaningful changes. How far any compromise could go would depend on “how much Infantino is willing to cede” and how much his opponents were willing to fight to take away, the world football executive said. There is historical irony in such an outcome. Reforms introduced after the downfall of former FIFA chief Sepp Blatter were intended in part to reduce the power concentrated in the presidency. Yet senior figures now see another battle developing over how much authority the FIFA president should wield. If no settlement is reached, the alternative could be attritional rather than spectacular. The world football executive said clubs could fight FIFA over the Club World Cup, financial distributions and player release; player representatives could challenge the calendar; national associations could obstruct initiatives; and major confederations could contest attempts to expand or reshape FIFA competitions. “Maybe it seems like we’re boiling down to two options now,” the executive said. “One, a compromise where Gianni gives up some of his power and there are some new bodies that are created or, two, a permanent hot-cold war where all the stakeholders just fight every issue.” That could include expanded World Cups, bigger or more frequent Club World Cups and commercial distribution decisions, the executive said. The result would not necessarily be a formal break with FIFA. Instead, opponents could make every major initiative harder to deliver. The veteran sports executive said the challenge went to the heart of how global governing bodies function. “The importance of unity. Keeping these monster sports organisations together, they are not political parties,” the executive said. “This will be new territory.” INFANTINO REBUILDS There is another reason the focus is shifting towards life with Infantino rather than replacing him: his position appears to have strengthened since the crisis first erupted. A national association president, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity, believes Infantino’s opponents missed their best opportunity when the backlash was at its peak and that he is now rebuilding support ahead of the March election. The FIFA president has a succession of opportunities in the coming months to meet national association leaders at tournaments, congresses and confederation events, including several gatherings in Africa. The association president expects Infantino to use those meetings to maintain support among football leaders through to the FIFA presidential election in March 2027. The political significance of smaller associations has also been highlighted by a proposal from Ceferin and CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani for FIFA to distribute at least $10 million from its [USN:L6N45A0ZG TEXT:"reserves"] to each of its 211 member associations during the next financial cycle. For many associations heavily reliant on FIFA funding, such sums could be transformative. If Infantino is reelected, the association president believes some federations that have opposed him may eventually become less hostile, concluding there is little to gain from four years of permanent confrontation. That possibility means a "cold war" is not inevitable.

item.title: White House reinstates access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico following judge's order
item.description: The White House said on Thursday it has reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge deemed US President Donald Trump's ban of the three news outlets likely unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey, Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: The White House said on Thursday it has reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge deemed US President Donald Trump 's [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"ban of the three news outlets"] likely unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored. The midday reinstatement came after a chaotic few hours earlier on Thursday when the journalists continued to be blocked from entering the White House grounds. That prompted the three news organizations to request an immediate hearing before US District Judge Tim Kelly, who issued his decision overnight. Kelly, acting in a lawsuit brought by CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Monday, ordered a halt to Trump's ban for 14 days in a press freedom case that has played out over the past week in the courtroom and White House grounds. Kelly found that the revocation of the White House credentials of the journalists "likely violated their constitutional due process rights." The judge, who Trump appointed in 2017 during his first presidential term, also raised doubts about the US Justice Department's national security arguments for justifying the ban, noting that Trump himself had said the action was due to what the president alleged was false or negative coverage. Hours after Kelly issued his order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico told the judge they remained barred, and asked for the emergency hearing. Politico said its reporter's credentials were confiscated. An MS NOW reporter said she was blocked from the White House. CNN said some of its staff members were denied entry onto the grounds. In response, Micah Stopperich, the director of press operations at the White House, said in a court filing that the White House began the process of reinstating press badges for affected reporters at 7:25 a.m., and that the "White House press team dropped badges at the entry gate for members of the press to pick up around 9:55 a.m." After receiving Stopperich's declaration, the judge denied the request by the news organizations for an emergency hearing but gave them an opportunity to inform him of any factual developments later in the day. The sharpest conflict yet between Trump and the press played out during a key diplomatic moment for the US president: his appearance at the United Nations General Assembly in New York and his hosting of Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. It was unclear whether members of the White House television press pool would reinstate their coverage following CNN’s return to the White House. Earlier this week, they had suspended pooled coverage in solidarity with CNN. There were no TV pool cameras set up for Xi's arrival on the White House's South Lawn on Thursday morning, and FOX News, MS NOW and CNN did not air the two leaders' arrival ceremony live. During Trump's welcome of Xi to the White House, the president made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about the Chinese having the friendliest press corps. CNN is one of the five news organizations – along with ABC, CBS, FOX News and NBC – that make up the primary White House television pool. They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organizing coverage and provide footage to other outlets. CNN had been scheduled to cover Trump's trip to New York for the General Assembly on Monday, but was not able to provide a pool feed. NATIONAL SECURITY CONCERNS Trump announced the ban on Friday on his social media platform, saying those news organizations "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." Trump framed their reporting as a threat to US national security. The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the three news outlets. Kelly ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and stop enforcing the ban for two weeks. The judge rejected the administration's stated national security concerns. "The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds," Kelly wrote. In a filing on Tuesday, the Justice Department accused the outlets of threatening national security with their coverage, citing stories about US missile stockpiles, construction of Trump's White House ballroom and turnout at the recent Republican midterm convention. Theodore Boutrous, an attorney for the three outlets, welcomed the judge's decision in a statement, saying: "This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court's swift action." TENSIONS WITH THE PRESS Although other presidential administrations have battled with the press, Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. Upending decades of tradition, his White House had denied basic access to many major news organizations, launched personal attacks on journalists and filed multiple lawsuits against news organizations. Kelly's ruling came a day after Trump experienced another legal setback. On Wednesday, an Iowa judge [USN:L4N45F1L5 TEXT:"dismissed"] Trump's 2024 lawsuit against the Des Moines Register newspaper and pollster J. Ann Selzer. Trump sued the Register, its parent company Gannett and Selzer over a poll published ahead of the November 2024 US election that showed Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris leading him in Iowa. Trump accused the newspaper and its longtime pollster of fraudulently misleading readers. In his ruling Wednesday, Iowa District Judge Scott Beattie said the poll was legally protected speech.

item.title: Macklemore sets 'Free Palestine' tour after being dumped from Ed Sheeran shows
item.description: American rapper Macklemore, who was dropped as the opening act for Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks, announced on Thursday he would headline his own "Free Palestine" concert tour that will start next month.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: American rapper Macklemore, [USN:L4N4561KP TEXT:"who was dropped"] as the opening act for Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks, announced on Thursday he would headline his own "Free Palestine" concert tour that will start next month. The tour will begin in Dublin, Paris and London, Macklemore said in an Instagram post. US dates and additional performers will be announced later, he said, adding that proceeds would be donated to organizations that support the Palestinian people. "Being apolitical during a genocide doesn't work anymore," he said. "People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it." The Grammy-winning rapper had been due to perform at eight additional Sheeran shows when he was removed last month from the tour following remarks at a show in New Jersey. "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: 'Free Palestine,'" he said on stage. Macklemore said owners of stadiums where Sheeran was set to play had objected to those remarks. Israeli officials have strongly denied their actions in Gaza amount to genocide and say they are justified as self-defense. Sheeran, an English-born singer-songwriter and one of the world's top-selling recording artists, said the decision to dump Macklemore came from tour organizers, not him, and that he tried to find a resolution. He [USN:L1N4570VJ TEXT:"apologized for his handling of the situation"] at a performance in Philadelphia and decried Israel's treatment of residents in Gaza as "unjustifiable." Macklemore has been an outspoken critic of Israel's assault on Gaza and its [USN:L6N42H0E8 TEXT:"occupation of the West Bank"]. "If these last couple of weeks have shown us anything, it's that something has shifted over the last three years," Macklemore said on Thursday. "There has been a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now." "What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," he added. "When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."

item.title: Rússia tem menos compradores de trigo devido à paralisação do comércio no Mar Negro
item.description: Menos países estão comprando trigo russo depois que os ataques da Rússia e da Ucrânia no Mar Negro mantiveram fechada uma importante rota de exportação desde julho, segundo dados divulgados na quarta-feira pela União Russa de Grãos.
item.dc:creator: Olga Popova
item.content:encoded: Menos países estão comprando trigo russo depois que os ataques da Rússia e da Ucrânia no Mar Negro mantiveram fechada uma importante rota de exportação desde julho, segundo dados divulgados na quarta-feira pela União Russa de Grãos. Os dados mostraram que apenas oito países compraram trigo da Rússia, o maior exportador mundial de trigo, em setembro, contra 26 no ano anterior. Em agosto, o número de compradores caiu para 16, ante 43 no mesmo mês de 2025. Yelena Tyurina, analista-chefe da União Russa de Grãos, disse à Reuters que o Egito continuava sendo o maior comprador de trigo russo, mas que suas compras entre 10 e 20 de setembro foram 3,6 vezes menores do que no ano anterior. Quênia e Iêmen foram os outros importantes compradores e também reduziram suas compras. Tyurina estimou que as exportações de trigo da Rússia totalizariam apenas 1 milhão de toneladas métricas em setembro, ante 5,7 milhões de toneladas em setembro de 2025. Os principais importadores de trigo na Ásia, no Oriente Médio e na África, que dependem dos suprimentos do Mar Negro, têm enfrentado dificuldades para garantir cargas, o que contribuiu para a alta dos preços. A Rússia está buscando redirecionar as exportações agrícolas para longe do Mar Negro, por meio de portos do Báltico e do Ártico, reaproveitando terminais de fertilizantes e carvão para movimentar grãos transportados por ferrovia a partir do sul da Rússia. A interrupção das exportações gerou um excedente no mercado interno, aumentou os estoques não vendidos e pressionou os preços locais para baixo. O banco central da Rússia alertou na quarta-feira que uma interrupção prolongada poderia afetar a produção agrícola. A consultoria Sovecon informou que o plantio de inverno está 14% abaixo do ritmo do ano passado. A empresa estimou que a área plantada até o momento é a menor para esta fase da safra desde 2013, quando chuvas intensas interromperam o plantio.

item.title: 英インフレリスク、冬場に顕在 早期利下げに慎重＝ディングラ中銀政策委員
item.description: [ロンドン ２４日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行、ＢＯＥ）金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）のディングラ委員は２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英インフレリスク、冬場に顕在　早期利下げに慎重＝ディングラ中銀政策委員 3:21 配信

２０２３年３月撮影　REUTERS/Hannah McKay

[ロンドン　２４日　ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行、ＢＯＥ）金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）のディングラ委員は２４日、米イラン情勢の緊迫化に伴う原油高に伴う英国の長期的なインフレ影響は、エネルギー需要が高まる冬場に顕在化するとの見方を示した。中期的なインフレ要因も年末までに明確になり始めるとし、早期利上げには慎重な姿勢を示した。

英シンクタンクの国立経済社会研究所（ＮＩＥＳＲ） の会議に出席したディングラ氏は、冬場にかけて「賃金交渉の行方や最終的水準についても、より多くのことが分かってくる。金融引き締めはすでに進行中だ」と述べた。

一方、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻を受けてエネルギー価格が急騰した２０２２年のような、広範囲にわたる物価上昇は起きておらず、雇用市場も弱含んでいると指摘した。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）や米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は利上げに動いているものの、英国の需要水準は米国を下回り、指標金利もユーロ圏よりも高いため、英中銀の据え置き決定は妥当だと主張した。ディングラ氏は、今月のＭＰＣで金利据え置きを支持していた。

人工知能（ＡＩ）の利用拡大がサービス部門でのインフレ鈍化につながる可能性があるとの見方も示したほか、英国の中期的なインフレ期待は懸念すべき状況ではないとした。

また、英中銀のロンバルデリ副総裁は２４日、景気減速が鮮明にならない限り、エネルギー価格の高止まりを受けて利上げが必要になるとの認識を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 9/25(金) 3:21 ロイター

item.title: Decenas de delegados abandonan sala de la ONU al inicio del discurso de Netanyahu
item.description: Decenas de delegados de las Naciones Unidas abandonaron la sala cuando el primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, comenzó su discurso ante la reunión de líderes mundiales de la Asamblea General el jueves .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Decenas de delegados de las Naciones Unidas abandonaron la sala cuando el primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, comenzó su discurso ante la reunión de líderes mundiales de la Asamblea General el jueves . Tras calificarlos de "cobardes morales", pidió a cualquiera que se sintiera así que se marchara antes de que él comenzara a hablar.

item.title: US Treasury accepted $4.078 billion in buyback operation
item.description: The US Treasury Department said on Thursday that it bought back $4.078 billion in 20- to 30-year bonds as part of its ongoing buybacks to support market liquidity. Bonds worth $10.468 billion were offered during the operation. The Treasury said earlier on Thursday that it would buy back up to $6 billion in the
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: The US Treasury Department said on Thursday that it bought back $4.078 billion in 20- to 30-year bonds as part of its ongoing buybacks to support market liquidity. Bonds worth $10.468 billion were offered during the operation. The Treasury said earlier on Thursday that it would buy back up to $6 billion in the debt.

item.title: 約80カ国が国連で共同声明、ホルムズ海峡の再開要求 イランとフーシ派非難
item.description: [国連 ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連　２４日　ロイター] - 世界の約８０カ国は国連で２４日、ホルムズ海峡の緊急再開を求めるとともに、同地域での攻撃や国際貿易・エネルギー安全保障の混乱を巡ってイランとその同盟勢力であるイエメンの武装組織フーシ派を非難した。

バーレーンのザヤーニ外相は共同声明で「ホルムズ海峡におけるイランの行動は、国際的な安全保障および航行の権利と自由を脅かし続けている」と指摘。「またイエメンでの紛争を再開させたフーシ派の決定、サウジアラビアへの継続的な攻撃、紅海における無謀な攻撃についても強く非難する」と述べた。

また、フーシ派がバベルマンデブ海峡に向けて進軍を続けていることは、国際的な海運、海上安全保障、世界貿易に対するリスクを一段と高めるだけだと非難した。

声明には、湾岸アラブ諸国をはじめ主要な西側諸国が賛同した。

item.title: One dead after security forces open fire during Ebola burial in Congo, sources say
item.description: One person was killed and several others wounded after security forces fired shots to contain unrest during the burial of a suspected Ebola victim in northeastern Congo on Thursday, two sources said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: One person was killed and several others wounded after security forces fired shots to contain unrest during the burial of a suspected Ebola victim in northeastern Congo on Thursday, two sources said. The incident occurred at Katula-Paida cemetery in Beni, a city in North Kivu province, which has recently seen a surge in Ebola infections. The burial team was preparing to bury the body in line with Ebola safety procedures when residents demanded to see the deceased, questioning whether the person had died of Ebola, according to a member of the Ebola response team in the city. Tensions escalated and security forces escorting the burial team opened fire as they sought to contain the unrest, the source said. At least one person was killed and several others were injured, according to the response team member and a health official who asked to remain anonymous. Investigations are underway to establish the full toll and circumstances of the incidents, two health officials said. The incident is the latest in a series of attacks on burial teams and other Ebola responders, underscoring persistent mistrust among the population. The outbreak, declared on May 15, has infected 7,820 people and killed 3,779, according to government data released on Wednesday.

item.title: NLRB revives test limiting protections for workers' profane, racist outbursts
item.description: The National Labor Relations Board has ruled that an employer-friendly test for when workers can be disciplined over profane job-related speech or conduct is back on the books after a US appeals court found that the agency's Biden-era decision overruling it was invalid.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: The National Labor Relations Board has ruled that an employer-friendly test for when workers can be disciplined over profane job-related speech or conduct is back on the books after a US appeals court found that the agency's Biden-era decision overruling it was invalid. The 3-1 ruling issued by the board on Wednesday involving rubber manufacturer Lion Elastomers is unusual because the NLRB generally does not treat [USN:L1N3J114G TEXT:"appeals court decisions"] as binding on its own decision-making, under a decades-old policy known as non-acquiescence. In 2023, a Democratic board majority used the case to [USN:L1N36Y1HX TEXT:"overrule a 2020 decision"] involving General Motors that had [USN:L2N2ES2AJ TEXT:"limited protections"] when workers engage in profane or discriminatory conduct in the course of a workplace dispute. But the New Orleans-based 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals in 2024 said that was improper and vacated the NLRB's decision. The board on Wednesday said that as a result, the 2023 ruling was never valid and the General Motors test remains good law that the NLRB can apply moving forward. "We find it impossible to reconcile the court's finding ... with any argument that General Motors remains overruled," the board wrote. The NLRB currently has [USN:L1N4430YP TEXT:"a 3-1 Republican majority"] appointed by President Donald Trump. Lawyers for Lion Elastomers and the union that represents its workers did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Thursday. NON-ACQUIESCENCE NLRB member David Prouty, the board's lone Democrat, dissented, accusing the majority of using the 5th Circuit decision to sidestep legal requirements that federal agencies engage in reasoned decision-making before adopting new legal standards. "My colleagues’ position swallows non-acquiescence whole [and] permits a single court decision to undo years of administrative work," Prouty wrote. The NLRB since at least the 1970s had analyzed on a case-by-case basis whether offensive speech or conduct [USN:L1N2ZL1B7 TEXT:"made in the course of a workplace dispute"] is protected by federal labor law. In its 2020 ruling in the General Motors case, the board had said it would instead look at whether employers would have taken the same action against a worker who made profane comments that did not involve a work-related dispute. Business groups including the US Chamber of Commerce applauded that ruling. They said that prior NLRB precedent had forced many employers to choose between violating labor law or violating laws requiring them to [USN:L1N3I22CY TEXT:"address workplace discrimination and harassment"]. But in 2023, the board in Lion Elastomers' case said labor disputes often become heated and overruled General Motors, adopting what it called a "setting-specific" test. Lion Elastomers disciplined and ultimately fired a worker in 2017 after he got into a heated exchange with managers about working conditions. The case had already reached the 5th Circuit in 2021, when the court remanded it to the NLRB to apply the General Motors standard. The company appealed the 2023 decision and the 5th Circuit ultimately vacated it and remanded the case again for the board to apply General Motors. The court did not address the merits of the issue, but said the board had exceeded the scope of its initial remand in 2021. The board's Republican members on Wednesday acknowledged that non-acquiescence is an established board policy, but said that because the 5th Circuit did not resolve the merits of the case they were not acquiescing to the court's interpretation of federal labor law. The case is Lion Elastomers, National Labor Relations Board, No. 16–CA–190681. For Lion Elastomers: Steven Cupp of Fisher Phillips For the NLRB general counsel: Colton Puckett For the union: Nathan Kilbert of United Steelworkers of America Read more: [USN:L1N3J114G TEXT:"NLRB protections for workers' 'abusive' conduct nixed by US court"] [USN:L1N36Y1HX TEXT:"U.S. labor board raises bar to discipline workers for 'abusive' conduct"] [USN:L2N2ES2AJ TEXT:"NLRB limits protections for profane, racist outbursts by workers"] [USN:L1N2ZL1B7 TEXT:"Worker's firing over vulgar comment violated labor law, court rules"] [USN:L1N3I22CY TEXT:"EEOC warned by Republican lawmaker against protecting 'offensive' worker conduct"] [USN:L1N1KV00V TEXT:"8th Circuit upholds workers' rights to make racist comments while picketing"]

item.title: GM, Ford to see US market-share slide, forecaster predicts
item.description: General Motors and Ford Motor have lost more market share in the United States than any other automakers so far this year as buyers prioritize fuel efficiency amid high gas prices, an industry forecast shows.
item.dc:creator: Kalea Hall
item.content:encoded: General Motors (GM.N) and Ford Motor have lost more market share in the United States than any other automakers so far this year as buyers prioritize fuel efficiency amid high gas prices, an industry forecast shows. Ford’s vehicle sales are expected to drop 8.8% through the first three quarters of the year, according to a forecast released Thursday from Cox Automotive. That would knock Ford’s market share down nearly a full percentage point, to 12.5%. GM’s US vehicle sales pace also is trailing the broader industry, expected to decline 6.2% year-to-date through September 30, Cox projects. The firm estimates GM will finish the quarter with a 16.7% market share, down from 17.4% a year earlier. Those would be the two steepest market-share declines among 13 car companies tracked by Cox, according to its quarterly forecast. Chrysler-parent Stellantis, the other one of the traditional three Detroit carmakers, is expected to gain market share through the third quarter. Still, the overall share of the three companies is expected to be at an all-time low of around 36%, Cox said. Analysts say both GM and Ford are being hurt by a relative lack of fuel-efficient cars and SUVs, compared to rivals. A GM spokesman declined to comment. CAR BRANDS WITH HYBRIDS GAIN GM dealers have said some of their customers have switched to other brands because [USN:L6N4570VU TEXT:"GM doesn’t offer hybrid models"]. Ford’s sales declined in part after it discontinued its popular Escape compact SUV, one of its most fuel-efficient offerings. Ford’s overall sales also have been pressured this year by lower pickup-truck production after a [USN:L6N3YY0QZ TEXT:"fire at an aluminum supplier"] cut output. Automakers with several hybrid models - which combine a gas engine with an electric motor and battery to save fuel - have fared better this year amid higher gas prices stemming from the Iran war. Sales from Hyundai (005380.KS) and Kia (000270.KS) combined are expected to surpass Ford’s sales in the third quarter, which would be the first time the sibling South Korean automakers sold more cars than Ford in any quarter, according to Cox. In a statement Ford said Hyundai and Kia are two separate companies and "even lumped together, Ford outsold the two Korean companies combined year to date. By revenue, the gap between Ford and Hyundai Kia is much higher." Toyota, the industry’s leader in hybrid sales, is expected to post a 1.1% sales gain through three quarters. Honda’s sales are expected to be up 5.6%, Cox said. “We see some of these Asian brands coming forward and really taking the industry by storm,” said Erin Keating, Cox executive analyst. “Most importantly, they have the hybrids.” Overall, US consumers are weathering tough economic pressures. Cox forecasters upped their US vehicle sales expectations to 16.1 million for the year, from an earlier forecast of 15.8 million. “Despite this volatile year, the new vehicle market has actually held up surprisingly steady,” Keating said.

item.title: Raphinha se reinventa no Barcelona e Deco diz que "Julián Álvarez é passado”
item.description: O diretor esportivo do Barcelona, Deco, descartou definitivamente a possibilidade de retomar a busca pelo atacante Julián Álvarez, nesta quinta-feira, após uma ofensiva que terminou em frustração e, de forma inesperada, abriu caminho para uma nova função de Raphinha como centroavante.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: O diretor esportivo do Barcelona, Deco, descartou definitivamente a possibilidade de retomar a busca pelo atacante Julián Álvarez, nesta quinta-feira, após uma ofensiva que terminou em frustração e, de forma inesperada, abriu caminho para uma nova função de Raphinha como centroavante. O Barcelona passou o período entre temporadas em busca de um “número nove” após a saída de Robert Lewandowski, que se transferiu para a Major League Soccer, tendo o capitão da Inter de Milão, Lautaro Martínez, e Álvarez, do Atlético de Madri, no topo da lista de prioridades. Mas Deco, em declarações à imprensa no Portugal Football Summit, afirmou que ambas as tentativas não deram em nada. “A ideia sempre foi trazer um atacante com boa movimentação e capacidade de se entrosar com os demais, e Julián (Álvarez) era um desses jogadores”, disse Deco. “Não foi possível; fizemos uma oferta... o clube sempre disse que não o venderia, então temos que buscar outras soluções.” “Julián (Álvarez) é passado; temos que olhar para frente, e estamos felizes. Espero que ele também esteja indo bem, que esteja ajudando seu clube”, acrescentou Deco ao ser questionado se o clube voltaria a tentar contratar o argentino na janela de transferências do meio da temporada. O presidente do Barcelona, Joan Laporta, havia falado publicamente sobre o interesse do clube em Álvarez no período entre temporadas, provocando uma reação irritada do presidente do Atlético de Madri, Miguel Ángel Gil Marín, que acusou o clube catalão de desonestidade e afirmou que o argentino “jamais” seria vendido para eles. O Barcelona acabou contratando Gabriel Jesus como opção de rodízio para o elenco de Hansi Flick, mas a solução surpreendente veio de dentro do próprio time, com o capitão Raphinha passando de sua função híbrida de meio-campista ofensivo e ponta-direita para a posição de centroavante. O jogador da seleção brasileira explodiu nessa função, marcando 14 gols em oito partidas, sendo 12 em sete jogos da LaLiga, assumindo a liderança da artilharia à frente de Lamine Yamal e Kylian Mbappé. “Estamos felizes porque descobrimos uma nova faceta de Raphinha”, disse Deco. “Mas o mais importante é que ele também está feliz." “É diferente para ele, porque às vezes não está em contato com a bola o tempo todo como costumava estar. Ele precisa estar preparado para atacar por trás dos zagueiros... Esperávamos que ele se saísse bem, mas não a esse nível.” Deco disse que Lautaro também havia sido seriamente considerado, mas o Barcelona rapidamente desistiu assim que a Inter deixou claro que seu capitão não estava disponível. “Em determinado momento, entre os atacantes que estávamos analisando, Lautaro era uma das opções”, afirmou Deco. “No momento em que o clube nos informou que ele não estava disponível, nem sequer tentamos ou discutimos o assunto mais a fundo.”

item.title: EUA e Irã discutem acordo em etapas para reabrir Estreito de Ormuz e encerrar bloqueio dos EUA, dizem fontes
item.description: Negociadores dos EUA e do Irã em Nova York estão explorando um caminho gradual para sair da guerra, que envolveria a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz por Teerã e o fim do bloqueio econômico imposto por Washington ao Irã, segundo fontes próximas às negociações.
item.dc:creator: Samia Nakhoul, Parisa Hafezi, John Irish
item.content:encoded: Negociadores dos EUA e do Irã em Nova York estão explorando um caminho gradual para sair da guerra, que envolveria a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz por Teerã e o fim do bloqueio econômico imposto por Washington ao Irã, segundo fontes próximas às negociações. O estreito tornou-se a principal moeda de troca nos esforços para pôr fim ao conflito de quase sete meses entre os EUA e o Irã, com o Irã buscando alívio do bloqueio norte-americano que está sufocando sua economia e Washington buscando livre passagem para navios na rota global de abastecimento de petróleo, atualmente bloqueada por Teerã. As negociações enfrentam um grande obstáculo, já que nenhum dos lados quer ser o primeiro a abrir mão de sua vantagem, segundo comentários à Reuters feitos por duas fontes iranianas, duas autoridades regionais e duas fontes diplomáticas ocidentais; no entanto, por trás da postura do Irã está o reconhecimento do custo econômico de um confronto prolongado. Uma autoridade sênior iraniana afirmou que a maneira mais plausível de pôr fim ao impasse seria um acordo em fases, com o Irã permitindo a navegação pelo Estreito de Ormuz em troca do levantamento do bloqueio econômico pelos EUA e de Teerã potencialmente obter acesso aos ativos congelados. “Um caminho a seguir seria resolver a crise em etapas. A primeira seria acabar com o bloqueio e reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz”, disse a autoridade à margem da Assembleia Geral da ONU. Isso implicaria que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, aceitasse outra solução temporária, após o fracasso de um acordo anterior em julho. Assim, um desafio central enfrentado pelos negociadores não é apenas esboçar um acordo, mas também garantir que quaisquer concessões sejam duradouras o suficiente para que ambos os lados confiem nelas, disseram as fontes. Trump disse acreditar que os EUA e o Irã poderiam chegar a um acordo após as eleições de meio de mandato para o Congresso, em 3 de novembro. Uma autoridade sênior europeia disse que os iranianos “têm uma lista muito longa de exigências”. Uma autoridade da Casa Branca disse que, embora “o Irã esteja desesperado por um acordo, o presidente Trump detém todas as cartas e tomará a decisão que for melhor para os Estados Unidos”. Trump, disse ele, continuava “aberto a dialogar com o Irã nas circunstâncias certas”, mas não tinha necessidade de negociar, e os EUA estavam em uma “posição muito forte”, com o controle do Estreito de Ormuz e uma economia iraniana que estava “entrando em colapso”. A autoridade disse que “sanções esmagadoras” e “um dos bloqueios mais bem-sucedidos da história” paralisaram a economia do Irã e deixaram o país completamente falido. Trump estava satisfeito em deixar que o “inevitável colapso iraniano” se desenrolasse, em vez de ser “manipulado” por Teerã, afirmou a autoridade. O ex-negociador norte-americano Dennis Ross disse que via apenas 30% de chance de se chegar a um acordo antes da votação, mas que ambos os lados podem ter motivos mais fortes para fechar um acordo antes do que depois das eleições de meio de mandato. “O bloqueio é o que realmente está pressionando os iranianos. Está estrangulando-os”, disse Ross. Um acordo antes das eleições de meio de mandato poderia beneficiar Trump, já que a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz poderia aliviar as tensões no Golfo, conter os preços do petróleo e ajudar a reduzir os preços da gasolina nos EUA, que são politicamente sensíveis. As chances do Irã obter o alívio econômico tão necessário podem ser maiores enquanto Trump ainda tiver um incentivo político maior para chegar a um acordo. Após as eleições de meio de mandato, disse Ross, Trump pode enfrentar menos restrições e estar mais disposto a intensificar a pressão ou considerar opções militares. FORÇA DE NEGOCIAÇÃO COMO OBSTÁCULO? A vantagem que trouxe Washington e Teerã de volta às negociações também pode tornar o acordo mais difícil. Washington controla a pressão que mais prejudica Teerã, enquanto Teerã controla o acesso a um ponto-chave estratégico de energia. Nenhum dos lados quer abrir mão dessa vantagem sem obter algo tangível em troca. Isso significa que as eleições de meio de mandato podem ser menos um prazo para a diplomacia do que para preservar as condições que tornam os esforços diplomáticos possíveis. Se Washington e Teerã não conseguirem transformar essa vantagem em um acordo antes das eleições de meio de mandato, a janela diplomática poderá se estreitar à medida que o risco de escalada cresce. Mesmo enquanto busca uma saída diplomática, Teerã está se preparando para a possibilidade de uma nova guerra com Washington, disse a autoridade iraniana, acusando os EUA de usar o bloqueio econômico e a ameaça de uso da força como ferramentas de coerção. “Nossos dedos estão no gatilho”, disse a autoridade sênior iraniana. “Os norte-americanos sabem o que precisam fazer, mas, devido às suas exigências excessivas, as chances de a diplomacia resolver isso são extremamente baixas.” Fontes regionais afirmaram que o governo iraniano estava disposto a retirar do acordo principal a exigência de pagamento de taxas de trânsito para usar o Estreito de Ormuz e, em vez disso, incluir essa exigência em um anexo, já que o fim do bloqueio havia se tornado a prioridade mais urgente. Os países do Golfo Pérsico rejeitaram a proposta de pagamento de taxas de trânsito. Qualquer acordo seria temporário, não um abandono formal da posição do Irã, afirmaram as fontes regionais. Os EUA intensificaram o cerco econômico ao Irã, impondo novas sanções além de um bloqueio que sufocou as exportações de petróleo do país, uma importante fonte de moeda forte. Neste mês, os EUA visaram as companhias aéreas comerciais restantes do Irã e suas redes de apoio, como parte de uma campanha para cortar os laços econômicos que sustentam o governo e a poderosa Guarda Revolucionária. Trump alertou que a economia do Irã poderia “apodrecer” caso não chegasse a um acordo. “O Irã não está focado principalmente em cobrar pedágios no Estreito de Ormuz, mas em preservar seu controle administrativo da via navegável”, disse ele. “O Irã pode estar disposto a adiar a questão do pedágio, mas não vai abrir mão do controle administrativo do estreito.” No cerne da diplomacia em Nova York há uma tensão fundamental. Washington quer que a pressão leve a concessões, Teerã quer que a pressão seja removida antes de fazê-las, e os países do Golfo querem que o conflito seja resolvido sem permitir que as vias navegáveis estratégicas da região se tornem moedas de troca duradouras. TEMORES DE UM CONFLITO SEM FIM Durante uma reunião separada com Trump em Nova York, os líderes do Golfo buscaram clareza sobre os planos finais de Washington após as eleições de meio de mandato, inclusive sobre se os EUA retomariam ações militares caso o Irã se recusasse a voltar às negociações. Eles expressaram sua rejeição coletiva a qualquer controle iraniano sobre o Estreito de Ormuz, afirmando que a liberdade de navegação deve ser restaurada e que a via navegável estratégica não deve se tornar uma ferramenta de coação contra os países do Golfo, segundo fontes regionais. No entanto, ao mesmo tempo em que alertaram sobre o Estreito de Ormuz, os líderes do Golfo pressionaram fortemente por uma redução da tensão e por um processo político, refletindo a determinação da região em permanecer fora de qualquer novo conflito entre os EUA e o Irã. “Ainda não está claro qual é o objetivo final de Trump, nem qual seria a alternativa à campanha de pressão”, disse Ebtessam al-Ketbi, presidente do think tank Emirates Policy Center, com sede em Abu Dhabi. “Os iranianos, por outro lado, sabem o que querem. Estão remodelando o cenário regional por meio de Ormuz e Bab el-Mandeb com um objetivo claro, enquanto Washington ainda não definiu seu plano de ação”, disse ela, referindo-se ao Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, que liga o Mar Vermelho ao Golfo de Áden. Essa incerteza também está moldando os cálculos de Teerã. Danny Citrinowicz, analista regional e ex-oficial da inteligência militar israelense, disse que as negociações em Nova York não alteraram as posições básicas de nenhum dos lados e que era improvável que o Irã recuasse enquanto acreditasse que Trump quisesse evitar uma escalada mais ampla antes das eleições de meio de mandato. “O bloqueio está prejudicando-os, mas, em vez de amenizar sua posição, é provável que os leve a intensificar o conflito, pois acreditam que, se abrandarem sua posição, estarão perdidos”, disse Alan Eyre, ex-negociador dos EUA para o Irã. Uma autoridade ocidental a par das negociações acrescentou: “Tudo se resume à abertura do Estreito de Ormuz. Estamos todos sob pressão interna e os iranianos sabem disso.”

item.title: Swiss lawmakers reflect shift on banks with UBS capital decision
item.description: A decision by Swiss lawmakers to defy calls by UBS and big business to moderate new banking rules has highlighted misgivings about the risks posed by one of the country's most visible institutions after the 2023 collapse of Credit Suisse.
item.dc:creator: Dave Graham
item.content:encoded: A [USN:L8N45F0DE TEXT:"decision"] by Swiss lawmakers to defy calls by UBS (UBSG.S) and big business to moderate new banking rules has highlighted misgivings about the risks posed by one of the country's most visible institutions after the 2023 collapse of Credit Suisse. Wednesday's upper house vote in favour of increasing the amount of capital Zurich-based UBS, which has a bigger balance sheet than the Swiss economy, must hold to back its foreign units went further than many political analysts had expected. "People are thoroughly fed up. It wasn't a vote of conviction, it was about fear of their own voters," said Cedric Wermuth, co-leader of Switzerland's Social Democrats. After two major banking crises inside two decades, the vote showed pressure had reached the point where parliament could not ignore popular demand for stricter rules, he told Reuters. Most upper house lawmakers belonging to parties either on the centre, centre-right or right of the political spectrum joined left-wingers in voting to make UBS back its foreign subsidiaries with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital over a more moderate plan that would have cost the bank less. Speaking in support, Centre party lawmaker Pirmin Bischof said Credit Suisse's downfall made it vital that Switzerland try to ensure it could never happen again. The vote followed a lengthy consultation process in which Swiss cantons and business groups had urged the government to keep the capital requirements in line with other major financial centres, raising concerns about Switzerland's competitiveness. A Swiss poll published in June [USN:L8N42Q10X TEXT:"found"] 79% of respondents clearly or somewhat backed tougher capital requirements, even if it meant UBS paying lower dividends or having to accept less growth. Just 9% took the opposite view. Jakob Tanner, a history professor at the University of Zurich, said scepticism had been fuelled by the billions of dollars in bonuses paid out by Credit Suisse between 2010 and 2022 even as it racked up the losses that eventually sank it. A recent study published by the Swiss Bankers Association showed that while 53% of the population took a positive view of banks in 2025, this was down from 75% in 2021. Although the Swiss lower house must still debate the capital plan drawn up by Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter in response to the demise of Credit Suisse, many analysts view it as a bigger hurdle for UBS, which bought its historic rival. UBS, whose role in stabilising Switzerland's financial sector by acquiring Credit Suisse is often acknowledged by lawmakers, declined to comment. After the vote, it said the decision disregarded serious concerns expressed by business representatives, employee associations and most Swiss cantons. LOBBYING The Swiss National Bank and financial regulator FINMA both supported Keller-Sutter's original plan to make UBS back its foreign units with 100% CET1 capital. At present it must back those units with 60% capital, and is not limited to only using CET1. Several lawmakers had initially expressed confidence that a compromise passed in late August that would allow UBS to back its foreign units with 50% CET1 capital and cheaper 50% Additional Tier 1 (AT1) capital, would clear the upper house. But during lengthy debate in parliament last week it became clear the 90% CET1 plan was gaining ground and the final decision was pushed into this week. UBS set about rallying support for the AT1 option, with its chairman Colm Kelleher [USN:L8N4590WE TEXT:"warning"] the bank would have to consider its future in Switzerland if the new rules were too harsh. Switzerland's top business lobbies wrote to lawmakers urging them not to overregulate UBS and to back the AT1 plan. Then, in a weekend interview, UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti condemned the 90% CET1 option as excessive and said regulators were partly to blame for Credit Suisse's demise. Klaus Stoehlker, a Zurich-based public relations consultant, said the UBS campaign appeared to have alienated both lawmakers and authorities responding to public concerns. Switzerland was now likely to be left with a weaker bank, fettered by stringent new rules that risked accelerating the decline of its financial sector, Stoehlker added.

item.title: Otan intensifica compartilhamento de informações de inteligência diante da ameaça da Rússia, diz comandante
item.description: A Otan está intensificando o compartilhamento de informações de inteligência em resposta a uma onda de sabotagens e outros incidentes aparentemente ligados à Rússia, mas deve permanecer “calma e confiante” de que é capaz de lidar com qualquer ameaça representada por Moscou, afirmou o comandante-chefe da aliança à Reuters nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Sabine Siebold
item.content:encoded: A Otan está intensificando o compartilhamento de informações de inteligência em resposta a uma onda de sabotagens e outros incidentes aparentemente ligados à Rússia, mas deve permanecer “calma e confiante” de que é capaz de lidar com qualquer ameaça representada por Moscou, afirmou o comandante-chefe da aliança à Reuters nesta quinta-feira. Os comentários do general da Força Aérea dos EUA Alexus Grynkewich foram feitos depois que o serviço de inteligência de defesa da Dinamarca alertou que a Rússia provavelmente intensificaria uma guerra híbrida — termo que abrange uma série de ataques abaixo do nível de um ataque militar convencional — contra o Ocidente nos próximos meses. O serviço dinamarquês acrescentou que havia “um risco baixo, mas crescente” de que Moscou pudesse lançar um ataque militar limitado contra um ou vários países da Otan que fazem fronteira com a Rússia. “É preocupante”, disse Grynkewich, comandante supremo aliado da Otan na Europa, referindo-se a uma série de incidentes nas últimas semanas, incluindo uma tentativa de ataque com drone no Aeroporto de Leipzig/Halle, na Alemanha, e um navio russo disparando sinalizadores contra um helicóptero militar dinamarquês. “Mas devemos manter a calma e a confiança de que, como aliança — a mais poderosa da história —, dispomos das ferramentas e dos mecanismos necessários para gerenciar esse risco”, acrescentou. Moscou tem negado repetidamente qualquer envolvimento em guerra híbrida ou operações de sabotagem em países da Otan, bem como qualquer plano para um confronto. É MELHOR PUTIN NÃO TENTAR UM ATAQUE "ENQUANTO EU ESTIVER NO COMANDO”, DIZ GENERAL Grynkewich falava em uma entrevista por telefone à Reuters a caminho de uma cerimônia de troca de comando na sede da Otan em Norfolk, Virgínia, onde um general do Exército britânico está assumindo o lugar de um vice-almirante da Marinha dos EUA. Questionado sobre o risco de um ataque russo limitado ao território da Otan, Grynkewich enfatizou a prontidão da aliança para qualquer contingência desse tipo, afirmando que tal desdobramento era “improvável, mas algo que não podemos descartar”. Grynkewich rejeitou sugestões de que o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, pudesse ver uma oportunidade de atacar a Otan, considerando que os EUA esgotaram grande parte de seu estoque global de mísseis de longo alcance de alta precisão na guerra contra o Irã, segundo pessoas familiarizadas com os dados. “De jeito nenhum. É melhor ele nem tentar isso enquanto eu estiver no comando”, disse ele, acrescentando que a Otan está bem posicionada para defender cada centímetro de seu território. “Se partirmos da fase em que nos encontramos e começarmos a ver ameaças emergentes, estou confiante de que disponho agora da autoridade necessária para tomar medidas que dissuadam qualquer agressão contra a aliança.” OTAN EM PLENA MUDANÇA À MEDIDA QUE EUROPEUS ASSUMEM MAIOR PAPEL A transferência do comando de Norfolk para um comandante europeu faz parte de uma reorganização mais ampla, em consonância com as exigências do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de que as nações europeias assumam mais responsabilidade por sua própria segurança. Isso também significará que um europeu assumirá o comando da Força Conjunta da Otan em Nápoles. O Comando Conjunto de Forças da Otan em Norfolk é responsável pelas operações no Ártico e no norte da Europa, bem como pela proteção das rotas transatlânticas de reabastecimento. Na tentativa de tranquilizar os aliados europeus preocupados com uma revisão em andamento das forças norte-americanas no continente, Grynkewich afirmou que Washington continuaria “a fornecer capacidades essenciais, porém mais limitadas”, à Otan, à medida que os europeus assumissem um papel mais importante. Ele afirmou que não havia “nenhum resultado predeterminado” quanto ao número de soldados norte-americanos que permaneceriam na Europa e “quais capacidades poderiam ser realocadas”. Atualmente, cerca de 80 mil soldados norte-americanos estão baseados no continente. Trump tem ameaçado repetidamente sair da Otan — que tem sido dominada pelos EUA desde sua fundação em 1949 —, acusando os europeus de serem aproveitadores em matéria de segurança.

item.title: US energy secretary seeks refiners' help amid narrow options to curb diesel price
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has contacted executives at several major American refiners in recent days to gauge support for a voluntary restriction on diesel exports as the Trump administration searches for an alternative to a short-term ban, according to three people familiar with the discussions.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has contacted executives at several major American refiners in recent days to gauge support for a voluntary restriction on diesel exports as the Trump administration searches for an alternative to a short-term ban, according to three people familiar with the discussions. The effort to enlist companies voluntarily underscores the limited options available to the White House amid surging fuel prices that are pushing inflation higher and beginning to ripple through the broader economy as crucial November midterm elections approach. The push to restrict diesel exports also creates a potential clash with shareholders of refiners that have enjoyed bumper [USN:L6N44711J TEXT:"profits"] this year. President Donald Trump's administration is under political pressure to lower diesel prices, but more aggressive measures such as an export ban could disrupt refinery operations and raise the price of other fuels, leaving officials searching for ways to increase domestic diesel supplies without creating new problems elsewhere. The US is the world's largest diesel exporter. Trump [USN:SPN45A01C TEXT:"said on Tuesday"] that he supported restricting diesel exports, a move that surprised senior officials and kicked off a search for alternative measures. Speaking in New York on Tuesday, Wright said banning exports [USN:L1N45F0H3 TEXT:"was a bad idea"] and he preferred a voluntary effort, but did not provide specifics. The people familiar with the discussions did not name the companies contacted by Wright and it was not immediately clear what type of voluntary reductions the administration was seeking or how such an arrangement would be monitored or enforced. It was also unclear how the request was received by an industry that is benefiting from strong demand and record export revenues. "The Trump administration, including Secretary Wright, continue to work closely together as they consider a variety of options to help lower energy costs for the American people," said Department of Energy spokesman Ben Dietderich, when asked about the administration's effort to get refiners to voluntarily limit exports. “Ultimately, President Trump will make the final decisions,” he added. US diesel prices have climbed to about $6.52 a gallon, according to AAA, as disruptions tied to the wars in Iran and Ukraine have tightened global supplies. US diesel inventories were below 97 million barrels last week, about 13% below the five-year seasonal average, according to Energy Information Administration data. SOME REPUBLICANS CALL FOR BAN Trump's call for restrictions follows growing pressure from his fellow Republicans in states reliant on farming and other diesel-intensive industries, where soaring fuel costs have become a political issue ahead of the midterm elections. Republican lawmakers including Iowa Senator Chuck Grassley and candidates in competitive races have called for restricting exports as a way to ease costs for farmers and other diesel users. The American Petroleum Institute and more than 30 business, energy and manufacturing groups urged Trump on Wednesday to reject calls to limit diesel and other fuel exports. The industry argues that US refiners, particularly those along the Gulf Coast, produce more diesel than the region consumes and rely on exports as an outlet for the surplus. Restricting those sales could fill storage tanks and force refiners to reduce the amount of crude they process, cutting production of diesel as well as gasoline and jet fuel. Alan Gelder, senior vice president for oil markets at consultancy Wood Mackenzie, said it could also increase the need for gasoline imports, potentially at higher costs. "The irony of a US diesel export ban is that it would likely increase costs for American consumers," Gelder said. "Cutting crude runs to manage the oversupply would shift the cost burden from diesel to gasoline, meaning a policy designed to bring relief at the diesel pump could end up driving prices higher at the gasoline pump." An export ban could lower prices in the short-term, but the drop could be temporary if refiners cut production to match demand, according to Bjorn Markeson, an economist at economic data firm IMPLAN. One industry source said enthusiasm for any kind of voluntary program was limited. Reuters contacted major US refining companies, including Marathon (MPC.N) , Valero (VLO.N) , Chevron (CVX.N) and ExxonMobil (XOM.N) , to ask about the calls for an export ban and their support for voluntary restrictions. Those companies did not immediately respond. Phillips 66 declined to comment on whether the company has been approached by the Energy Department. Citgo said it had provided information to the administration and warned restrictions could have significant consequences. “The consequences of a potential diesel export ban are serious, particularly for refiners in the US Gulf Coast,” the company said.

item.title: Los excampeones Joshua y Fury pelearán en Cardiff el 11 de diciembre
item.description: El tan esperado enfrentamiento entre los excampeones británicos de peso pesado Anthony Joshua y Tyson Fury tendrá lugar en Cardiff el 11 de diciembre, anunció el jueves el promotor Turki Alalshikh en redes sociales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El tan esperado enfrentamiento entre los excampeones británicos de peso pesado Anthony Joshua y Tyson Fury tendrá lugar en Cardiff el 11 de diciembre, anunció el jueves el promotor Turki Alalshikh en redes sociales. Fury y Joshua dominaron la categoría durante gran parte de la última década, pero nunca hubo un combate entre ambos para unificar todos los cinturones importantes. Posteriormente, ambos fueron derrotados por Oleksandr Usyk, quien se convirtió en el campeón indiscutible de peso pesado. "Durante 15 años nadie ha sido capaz de organizar este combate (…) Ahora puedo confirmar que Fury contra Joshua llegará al Reino Unido, tal y como prometí a los aficionados británicos al boxeo", publicó Alalshikh en X. Joshua y Fury se enfrentarán por el título vacante de peso pesado "Super" de la WBA, según informó la revista Ring Magazine. La publicación, propiedad de Alalshikh, también actúa como promotora del combate. El cinturón, que Usyk le arrebató a Joshua en 2021, quedó vacante tras la renuncia del ucraniano en junio. "Estoy inspirando a toda una generación", publicó Joshua en Instagram, en respuesta al anuncio del combate. Fury, de 38 años, viene de ganar a Mariusz Wach, mientras que Joshua, de 36 años, noqueó a Kristian Prenga en julio.

item.title: Hungary looking to extend US sanctions waiver on Russian energy
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar's government is looking to extend a one-year exemption from US sanctions for using Russian oil and gas that is due to expire in November, Foreign Minister Anita Orban told news website index.hu on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar's government is looking to extend a [USN:L6N3WJ0WM TEXT:"one-year exemption"] from US sanctions for using Russian oil and gas that is due to expire in November, Foreign Minister Anita Orban told news website index.hu on Thursday. The agreement was brokered between US President Donald Trump and right-wing Hungarian leader Viktor Orban, who lost power at an April election after 16 years in office. S&P Global, which affirmed Hungary's credit rating at BBB- with a negative outlook in May, says more than 90% of the country's oil and gas imports come from Russia via pipelines through Ukraine, Bulgaria and Serbia. Dependence on Russian imports is seen as a source of vulnerability for Hungary's energy-intensive economy amid broader efforts by the European Union to wean itself off Russian energy since the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Anita Orban said Budapest is working on an extension of the sanctions waiver beyond November, adding Hungarian energy group MOL (MOLB.BU) needs more time for technological changes to diversify energy sources. While Viktor Orban had maintained close ties with the Kremlin, Magyar's cabinet [USN:L8N4500HJ TEXT:"expelled 10 Russian diplomats"] from Hungary this month, saying they had acted in ways incompatible with their status.

item.title: Paul Weiss calls bid to disqualify law firm in sugar antitrust case ‘gamesmanship’
item.description: Law firm Paul Weiss urged a federal judge in Minnesota on Wednesday to reject a bid from Mondelēz and other major food manufacturers to disqualify the firm from defending Domino Sugar and its owner ASR Group in a group of lawsuits over alleged price-fixing in the sugar industry.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: Law firm Paul Weiss urged a federal judge in Minnesota on Wednesday to reject a bid from Mondelēz and other major food manufacturers to disqualify the firm from defending Domino Sugar and its owner ASR Group in a group of lawsuits over alleged price-fixing in the sugar industry. Here are the details: In its court filing , Paul Weiss denied the food [USN:L6N4510AK TEXT:"manufacturers’ claim"] that the firm has a conflict of interest based on its earlier effort to represent the companies as plaintiffs in the same litigation. The law firm said the lead Paul Weiss attorneys who pitched representing the food companies have since left the firm. Paul Weiss criticized the move to disqualify the firm as “strategic gamesmanship at its worst and entirely without merit.” ASR and Domino in a separate filing on Wednesday defended Paul Weiss and urged the court not to disqualify the firm. “ASR/Domino would lose the attorneys who know their business, the industry, and the issues better than anyone," they said. Mondelez, ASR and Paul Weiss did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The manufacturers in seeking to oust Paul Weiss argue that they provided confidential strategy and pricing data to the firm in 2024 when they were preparing to bring the case and the law firm was vying to represent them. Paul Weiss countered that the only information sent to the firm was "historical purchasing data from just one of the plaintiffs." Mondelez's lawsuit and a group of similar cases allege ASR and other sugar producers engaged in illegal price coordination. A judge last year [USN:L2N3VW0XO TEXT:"allowed"] groups of proposed class actions to advance. ASR and other defendants have denied any wrongdoing. The lead Paul Weiss attorneys who earlier sought to represent the food manufacturer plaintiffs, including William Isaacson, [USN:L1N3RV10O TEXT:"left the firm"] last year to open a new law firm. Paul Weiss became involved in the case as defense counsel for ASR and Domino in September last year, when Djordje Petkoski, the lead attorney for the companies, joined Paul Weiss from rival law firm A&O Shearman. Read more: [USN:L6N4510AK TEXT:"US judge urged to oust law firm Paul Weiss from sugar price-fixing case"] [USN:L6N453144 TEXT:"Law firm Quinn Emanuel wins fight over role in data center case"] [USN:L6N44P0QP TEXT:"Quinn Emanuel's conflict battles highlight thorny challenge for big law firms"] [USN:L6N44W0YH TEXT:"Law firm Quinn Emanuel ousted from defamation case against Muddy Waters"]

item.title: Anthropic e OpenEvidence firmam parceria para IA médica
item.description: A companhia de inteligência artificial Anthropic e a plataforma de conhecimento médico OpenEvidence anunciaram nesta semana parceria na área de ferramentas de diagnóstico baseado em IA.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: A companhia de inteligência artificial Anthropic e a plataforma de conhecimento médico OpenEvidence anunciaram nesta semana parceria na área de ferramentas de diagnóstico baseado em IA. A OpenEvidence tem recursos que respondem às perguntas dos médicos com base em pesquisas médicas revisadas por pares e diretrizes de tratamento. A plataforma é gratuita para profissionais da área médica nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá. A nova iniciativa trata-se de uma versão especializada disponível gratuitamente para profissionais de saúde em dezenas de países de baixa e média rendas, onde o acesso limitado à literatura médica, à expertise de especialistas e à educação médica continuada pode prejudicar o atendimento a pacientes. Sistemas de saúde em todo o mundo estão analisando se a IA generativa pode ajudar a lidar com a escassez de médicos e especialistas. Os defensores argumentam que as ferramentas de IA podem ajudar os profissionais da área médica a navegar rapidamente por vastas quantidades de informações médicas, enquanto os críticos alertam que sistemas treinados principalmente com dados de países de alta renda podem não refletir as condições locais de prática. A iniciativa está sendo implementada em cerca de 100 países, incluindo Uganda, Angola, Sudão, Haiti e Mongólia, de acordo com uma lista fornecida pela OpenEvidence. “O acesso ao conhecimento médico não deveria depender da localização geográfica”, afirmou Daniel Nadler, fundador da OpenEvidence. A Reuters noticiou na semana passada que a Anthropic montou um laboratório para realizar trabalhos de biologia, à medida que leva adiante suas ambições em inteligência artificial na área de ciência farmacêutica e enquanto o medo sobre o alcance da IA toma conta do público, com alguns executivos e políticos pedindo uma desaceleração no desenvolvimento. Anthropic e OpenEvidence não divulgaram os termos financeiros da parceria. DIFERENÇAS REGIONAIS Só em agosto, médicos dos EUA consultaram a OpenEvidence 42 milhões de vezes, segundo Nadler. Em 2026, várias centenas de milhões de norte-americanos terão sido tratados por um médico que utilizou a OpenEvidence para orientar o tratamento, disse ele. A tecnologia da Anthropic fornecerá suporte, enquanto a OpenEvidence adapta o sistema às diferentes regiões, levando em conta a infraestrutura de saúde, informaram as empresas. No início deste ano, a OpenEvidence informou que estava trabalhando com organizações de saúde em Ruanda e Botsuana para adaptar suas ferramentas a contextos em que os padrões de doenças, os recursos de diagnóstico e os tratamentos disponíveis diferem significativamente daqueles em países mais ricos. “Cem por cento do que estamos desenvolvendo para esses locais é adaptável ao contexto”, disse Nadler. Mesmo onde as unidades médicas não têm eletricidade 24 horas por dia, a maioria dos médicos possui smartphones, disse ele, o que significa acesso a informações médicas de qualidade que, há uma década, só estariam disponíveis em instituições de ponta. Ahmed Bendary, cardiologista da Universidade de Benha, no Egito, disse que ampliar esse acesso para além dos Estados Unidos e da Europa “será um enorme salto à frente, especialmente em regiões onde as assinaturas institucionais das principais revistas médicas são limitadas, tornando as ferramentas baseadas em evidências e de uso no local de atendimento ainda mais vitais”.

item.title: Airbus apresenta Eurofighter a Portugal como melhor substituto para caças F-16
item.description: A Airbus afirmou nesta quinta-feira que planeja apresentar uma proposta não solicitada a Portugal no final de outubro ou início de novembro para o fornecimento de caças Eurofighter Typhoon, visto que o país busca substituir sua frota obsoleta de F-16, apresentando o avião de combate de fabricação europeia como mais adequado às necessidades de Lisboa do que o F-35 da Lockheed Martin.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves
item.content:encoded: A Airbus (AIR.PA) afirmou nesta quinta-feira que planeja apresentar uma proposta não solicitada a Portugal no final de outubro ou início de novembro para o fornecimento de caças Eurofighter Typhoon, visto que o país busca substituir sua frota obsoleta de F-16, apresentando o avião de combate de fabricação europeia como mais adequado às necessidades de Lisboa do que o F-35 da Lockheed Martin. Portugal ainda não lançou uma licitação formal para substituir seus 28 caças F-16M modernizados, mas a iniciativa da Airbus sinaliza uma intensificação da competição por um acordo que fortaleceria os laços de defesa de Lisboa com parceiros europeus ou norte-americanos. A Airbus fabrica o Typhoon com a britânica BAE Systems (BAES.L) e o Leonardo da Itália (LDOF.MI) . A proposta incluiria "soluções de financiamento público e privado para Portugal, a fim de aliviar o plano de pagamento", juntamente com a participação industrial e a cooperação militar vinculadas à oferta, disse aos jornalistas Ivan Gonzalez Exposito, gerente da campanha do Eurofighter em Portugal. O chefe da Airbus Defence & Space na Europa, José Luis de Miguel, afirmou que Portugal também poderia se beneficiar de laços de defesa, políticos e industriais mais fortes com parceiros europeus importantes no programa Eurofighter. O ministro da Defesa de Portugal, Nuno Melo, afirmou que deseja ver a concorrência entre os fabricantes para maximizar os benefícios para o país e suas indústrias. O Typhoon enfrenta a concorrência do F-35 da Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , amplamente considerado pelos analistas de defesa como o principal concorrente, assim como o Rafale da Dassault Aviation e o Gripen E da Saab. González Exposito afirmou que as principais tarefas da Força Aérea Portuguesa se concentram no policiamento aéreo, em missões de alerta de reação rápida da Otan e na proteção do espaço aéreo e das águas nacionais, em vez de realizar operações ofensivas em território inimigo, que é o principal objetivo do caça furtivo F-35. "Para isso, o Eurofighter é a solução ideal", disse ele, descrevendo-o como "o melhor caça de superioridade aérea do mundo".

item.title: BP eyes Devon Energy asset amid renewed US M&A ambitions, sources say
